rules.name: Declaring the Minor
rules.desc: To declare the FGSS minor, the student must first email the Assistant Director of Student Services, who will guide the student through the steps of declaration. The student then must meet with the Director of Undergraduate Studies or the Faculty Director to develop and review their study plan. As the final step, the student declares the Minor on Axess.

rules.name: Core Required Course
rules.desc: Course must be taken for 4 or more units and a letter grade.

rules.name: Theory Requirement
rules.desc: Students must complete FEMGEN 103 or another approved theory course for 4 or more units and a letter grade.

rules.name: Minor Electives
rules.desc:
Minors designate a minimum of 16 units from any of the approved FGSS course lists below. Courses can be all from one list or from different lists.
Students may petition to count courses outside of the course lists with approval from the Faculty Director. Please contact the FGSS Faculty Director and Director of Undergraduate Studies to confer about which courses are appropriate for your focus.

children.name: Humanities and Arts Courses
children.desc: Humanities and Arts centers the arts, history, literature, language, media, and performance in the analysis of how ideas about feminism, gender, and sexuality are developed, produced, and experienced alongside other categories of difference.
children.notes: Note: Not all courses are offered every year. Students may take additional elective courses to meet the minimum unit requirement for the minor.

children.name: Queer and Transgender Studies Courses
children.desc: Queer and Transgender Studies focuses on the histories, practices, and theories of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, intersex, and queer identities and communities through multidisciplinary study.
children.notes: Note: Not all courses are offered every year. Students may take additional elective courses to meet the minimum unit requirement for the minor.

children.name: Technology, Science, and Medicine Courses
children.desc: Technology, Science, and Medicine investigates ethical considerations in how gender, sex, sexuality and other categories of embodied difference shape and are shaped by technology, science, and health and medicine in the application of scientific knowledge.
children.notes: Note: Not all courses are offered every year. Students may take additional elective courses to meet the minimum unit requirement for the minor.

children.name: Law and Social Sciences Courses
children.desc: Law and Social Sciences investigates how gender, sex, and sexuality and other categories of embodied difference are studied, regulated, and experienced in economics, politics, education, public policy, and the law.
children.notes: Note: Not all courses are offered every year. Students may take additional elective courses to meet the minimum unit requirement for the minor.
